title: console: repair tenant-specific dashboard tile no-data regression and tracing correlation during high-ingest incidents
creator: Maya Patel
description: During a sustained high-ingest window on 2025-03-11 tenant dashboards started showing intermittent "no data" tiles for metrics that still existed in raw storage and a breakdown in trace->metric correlation links. This triggered multiple customer escalations from Dedicated and Private tenants who could not rely on console charts during an outage. Initial triage shows a race between metric pre-aggregation pruning and the new aggregation snapshot writer which caused tombstoned metric series to be visible to the live query engine for a short period, and a secondary issue where trace stitching keys were being hashed with a non-deterministic salt during a maintenance deploy. The combination causes: 1) dashboard tiles render as no-data because live-queries filtered out results that were reclaimed; 2) trace links cannot join to metric events because the stitching key changed mid-ingest. This ticket coordinates the hotfix, validation, and rollout to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers and captures follow-ups for a permanent fix.

acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout shows <1% tenant dashboards returning no-data for previously healthy metrics during a synthetic high-ingest replay
Trace->metric correlation tests pass for 100% of synthetic traces in staging after deterministic-salt deploy
Hotfix deployed to Hosted and Dedicated with rollback tested and documented
Private deploy bundle created and validated on customer lab environment
proposed_fix: 1) Guard aggregation snapshot writer's deletion path with an ACK from the live-query snapshot manager so tombstones are not visible to the query layer until full swap; 2) Revert accidental per-process trace salt and compute deterministic salt derived from organization_id and environment to ensure stable stitching keys; 3) Add fallback live-query path to raw-time-series for short windows while snapshots converge.
rollback_plan: Revert console hotfix commit and restore previous snapshot writer behavior; for tracing revert the deterministic-salt change by reapplying previous deploy; have canary and prod rollback playbooks ready. Alert customers if rollback required and schedule immediate follow-up patch. Runbook steps included in link above.
